new: BrowseCraft checks once a day whether a newer version is out: a plain request for a small public file, with no cookies and nothing about you or your PC. Turn it off on chrome://browsecraft.

A security update opens a tab saying how many security fixes it brings, how serious they are and whether any is already being exploited, with a Download button. It opens at most once a day, at start-up, and "Skip this version" silences that version.
Other updates show quietly in the menu and on the About page.
After an update, a tab shows what is new, what was fixed and the security fixes applied, for every version since the one you had. Turn it off on chrome://browsecraft.
The full change history is on the BrowseCraft website.
BrowseCraft for Linux (x86-64) can be downloaded from the website too.
fixed: The About page credits the Chromium open source project and its authors again (it had been renamed along with the browser).
chrome://browsecraft is now simply "BrowseCraft": it holds sync, updates and What's new.
